body:
Thank for the feedback. The usecase in details: let's say you have a categories panel like so: ![2015-09-21-134540\_288x271\_scrot](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/123822/9991100/4ee10f80-6067-11e5-8e57-a120e8e46703.png) Then when there are no refinements because of the query, you would want to either: * hide the panel * display something like "no categories for current query" And that's not feasible right now. The issue with our current API is that we decided to give the user the ability to provide a template PER refinement instead of being able to give a full template like this: ```mustache
categories
{{#noRefinements}}No refinements dude!{{/noRefinements}} {{#refinements}}
{{title}}
{{/refinements}}
``` Possible solutions: * give a full template, but we again raise the issue of "how do we know where the user clicked?". Two solutions for this: * force data-attributes to be set for us to target click events. like `
` * provide full templates using http://wix.github.io/react-templates/ * provide events like .on('refinements') on refinement list where you can subscribe to them and check data.length === 0 First solution should be the chosen one because the "events" solution is a hack to solve something simple here. Thoughts @algolia/javascript ?
